title: Whether religion is a theological virtue distinct from faith
pass_a_gloss: Article XXIII. Whether religion is a theological virtue distinct from faith. 1. Thomas Aquinas (2a2ae q.81) teaches that religion is a moral virtue (not theological) by which due worship is rendered to God. Others make it a theological virtue distinct from faith. 2. We: Religion broadly taken includes whole worship of God, and so is not a virtue really distinct from faith, hope, and charity, but their exercise toward God. Strictly, as a special virtue directing acts of worship, it can be distinguished from faith, yet is not a theological virtue in the same way as faith, hope, and charity — because its formal object is not God as supernatural end by revelation, but due worship.
pass_b_english: Article XXIII. Whether religion is a theological virtue distinct from faith.
1. Aquinas makes religion a moral virtue (not theological) rendering due worship to God. Others call it a theological virtue distinct from faith.

2. Broadly, religion is whole worship of God — not really distinct from faith, hope, and charity, but their exercise toward God. Strictly, as directing worship, it can be told apart from faith, yet is not theological in the same sense as faith, hope, and charity: its formal object is due worship, not God as supernatural end by revelation.
source_text:
ART. XXIII.
An Religio sit virtus Theologica a Fide distincta.

1. Thomas Aquinas 2.2. q.81 docet religionem esse virtutem moralem (non theologicam), qua DEO cultus debitus redditur. Alii eam virtutem theologicam a fide distinctam faciunt.

2. Nos: Religio late sumpta includit totum DEI cultum, & sic non est virtus a fide, spe, charitate realiter distincta, sed earum exercitium erga DEUM. Stricte, ut virtus specialis dirigendi cultus actus, potest a fide distingui, non tamen est virtus theologica eodem modo quo fides, spes, charitas — quia objectum ejus formale non est DEUS ut finis supernaturalis per revelationem, sed cultus debitus.
